overview: Two major classes of vehicle for delivering foreign genetic material into cells, trading off simplicity for delivery efficiency.
genZNote: Plasmids knock politely. Viral vectors let themselves in.

aspects.label: Overview / Core Definition
aspects.valueA: A circular, non-viral DNA molecule engineered to carry and express a gene of interest inside a host cell.
aspects.valueB: A modified virus, stripped of pathogenic genes, engineered to deliver genetic material into host cells using its natural infection machinery.

aspects.label: Delivery Mechanism
aspects.valueA: Introduced via transfection methods (chemical, electroporation, or lipid-based), which are relatively inefficient in many cell types.
aspects.valueB: Delivered via natural viral entry and infection mechanisms, generally far more efficient, especially in hard-to-transfect cells.

aspects.label: Genomic Integration
aspects.valueA: Typically remains episomal (non-integrating) unless specifically designed otherwise.
aspects.valueB: Depends on virus type — retroviruses/lentiviruses integrate into the host genome; adenoviruses and AAV typically remain episomal.

aspects.label: Cargo Capacity
aspects.valueA: Can carry relatively large inserts, limited mainly by plasmid stability.
aspects.valueB: Limited by the packaging capacity of the viral capsid (e.g. AAV holds under 5 kb).

aspects.label: Safety Considerations
aspects.valueA: Generally considered lower risk — no viral components, minimal immune response.
aspects.valueB: Requires careful design to prevent replication competency and manage immune responses; integrating vectors carry insertional mutagenesis risk.

aspects.label: Common Examples
aspects.valueA: Bacterial expression plasmids, mammalian expression vectors for transient transfection.
aspects.valueB: Adeno-associated virus (AAV), lentivirus, adenovirus — widely used in gene therapy.

aspects.label: Key Distinguishing Feature
aspects.valueA: Non-viral, lower delivery efficiency, generally safer.
aspects.valueB: Viral machinery, higher delivery efficiency, more safety considerations.
